deep.reconstruction:
The page holds three unrelated layers: (A) a deleted prose start on physics at the top; (B) a numerical reduction for a bifilar magnetometer (formulas at left, logarithmic arithmetic at right); (C) a pencil prose draft on the connectivity of surfaces, which belongs with the previous page (folio 25r).

(A) Header, mostly struck. It reads roughly 'Wenn die Erscheinung der Doppel[brechung?] ... in einer (später zu erklärenden) Weise abhängig, in der andern als negative Elektricität ...'. It is a fragment of a physical (electrical) argument. The reading is too uncertain to reconstruct.

(B) Bifilar suspension and magnetometer.

Step 1, directive torque. The previous page set up a body hung on two threads of length r. Upper attachment points sit at distance g, lower at distance f, vertical separation h, total weight G. When the body is twisted by an angle v it rises by z, with (h-z)^2 = h^2 - (f g/2)(1-cos v) (in the full-separation convention; my restatement). For small z this gives z ≈ f g (1-cos v)/(4h). The potential G z then yields the restoring torque G f g sin v/(4h). Hence the directive force
  D = f g G/(4h),
where f and g are the full separations. This is Gauss's bifilar formula (Gauss 1837/38, Resultate aus den Beobachtungen des magnetischen Vereins). The previous page wrote x = f cos v but already carried the prefactor fg/(4h), so the notation shifted between full separation and half separation.

Step 2, oscillation time. The equation of motion from the previous page is K v'' + D sin v = 0, with K the moment of inertia. Gauss's oscillation time (half-period) is S = π sqrt(K/D). Riemann writes
  S = ππK/D = 4ππhK/(fgG).
This is really S^2, or else S denotes the squared time.

Step 3, a log-tangent by interpolation. The angle is φ = 44°50'29''.
- The table gives log tan 44°50' = 9.9974734 (10-characteristic). This checks exactly.
- The tabular difference per 30'' is 1263.3 units of the 7th decimal, i.e. 42.11 per second.
- Riemann multiplies 29 × 42.1 ≈ 1221 (the '29,42,1').
- Adding gives log tan φ = 9.9975955. This is correct: the exact value of log10 tan(45° - 571'') + 10 is 9.99759549.

Step 4, the scale constant. In the right column he adds:
  9.9975955 (log tan φ) + 0.3010300 (log 2) + 0.7114698 (log 5.146) = 11.0100953.
He writes this as 1,0100953 (the crossed '4,0100' is a discarded attempt). The antilog is 10.23518, written '1023518', so the constant is 10235 = 2·R·tan φ with R ≈ 5146 scale divisions.

Step 5, the reduction formula. A mirror deflection read as n scale divisions corresponds to an angle n/(2R). For the bifilar arrangement dT/T = cot φ · dθ (standard; interpretation mine), which gives
  T/T0 = 1 + (n + 8.160)/10235.
Here T is the horizontal intensity and 8.160 is a zero-point offset of the scale reading. The general form written above it,
  T/T0 = (M f g h0)/(M0 f0 g0 h) · r,
expresses how changes in magnetic moment and in thread geometry (f, g, h relative to reference values f0, g0, h0) enter, with r a remaining factor.

Step 6, side computations.
- The expression sin(A-P-p) + B sin(A-P-p-B+α) is a torque-balance expression in terms of scale or azimuth readings A, P, p and angles B, α.
- He computes 1.0100953 + 0.9014583 (= log 7.97) = 1.9115536, giving about 81.57.
- The struck d^2(r)/dt^2 expression and the circle sketch with an arrow (magnet with mirror and scale?) are mechanical scraps. The pentagram is a doodle.

(C) Analysis situs (draft for 'Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen', Crelle 54, 1857, §§ Lehrsätze aus der analysis situs). The heavily struck opening says that for the purpose at hand some distinctions about the kind of connectivity of surfaces are needed. The draft continues approximately: 'Wir denken uns [die Fläche/das Flächenstück] durch allmähliche Erweiterung von einem Punkte aus erzeugt und nehmen an, daß, wenn zwei Theile derselben an einander stoßen, sie zusammen[wachsen/fallen] ...'. This is an attempt to build a surface by growth from a point.

It then states the key lemma: if a surface T is cut by n1 cross-cuts q1 into a system T1 of m1 simply connected pieces, and by n2 cross-cuts q2 into a system T2 of m2 pieces, then m2 - n2 cannot be < m1 - n1. The published version reads 'n2 - m2 nicht > n1 - m1', which is the same statement.

Applying it both ways (with both systems simply connected) shows that n - m is an invariant of T. This is the invariance of the connectivity order that the previous page sets out to prove: a surface cannot be both n-fold and m-fold connected.
errors: S = ππK/D should read S^2 = π^2 K/D if S is Gauss's oscillation time S = π sqrt(K/D); either a slip or S is used for the squared time.

Notation for f, g changes between pages: previous page uses f as a radius (x = f cos v), but D = fgG/(4h) is correct only if f and g are full separations of the thread attachment points. Not an error in the final formula.
Crossed '4,0100' in the log sum is a discarded miscalculation; the corrected 1,0100953 is right.
The interpolation 29 × 42.1 = 1220.9 → 1221 and the resulting log tan 44°50'29'' = 9.9975955 are correct to the 7th decimal.

results.what: Directive force of a bifilar suspension D = fgG/(4h) and oscillation time S^2 = π^2 K/D = 4π^2 hK/(fgG)
results.modern_name: Bifilar pendulum / bifilar magnetometer restoring torque
results.usually_credited_to: C. F. Gauss (1837), Göttingen Magnetic Union; W. Weber

results.what: Reduction of bifilar-magnetometer scale readings to relative horizontal intensity: T/T0 = 1 + (n + 8.160)/10235, with 10235 = 2·R·tan φ, R ≈ 5146 scale divisions, φ = 44°50'29''
results.modern_name: Scale-value calibration of a variometer (relative intensity variation)
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss and Weber (Resultate aus den Beobachtungen des magnetischen Vereins, 1837-41)

results.what: Lemma: if T is cut by n1 cross-cuts into m1 simply connected pieces and by n2 cross-cuts into m2 pieces, then m2 - n2 ≥ m1 - n1; hence the connectivity order (n - m) is well defined
results.modern_name: Invariance of the connectivity number (first Betti number / Euler characteristic) under different cut systems
results.usually_credited_to: B. Riemann (1851 dissertation; 1857 Abelian functions paper)

deep.surprise_reason: The topological lemma is a draft of the published 1857 analysis-situs lemma, already credited to Riemann; the rest is routine Gauss-Weber bifilar-magnetometer reduction from his Göttingen physics seminar work. The only mild interest is seeing the drafts physically interleaved with magnetometer arithmetic.

checkable.asserts: Tabular difference ≈ 42.1 units of the 7th decimal per arc-second near 45° (29·42.1 ≈ 1221, 30·42.1 ≈ 1263)
Rise z ≈ f g v^2/(8h), i.e. z ≈ fg(1-cos v)/(4h), giving torque G fg sin v/(4h) = D sin v

transcription_corrections: 'tang φ = 9,9974734 +29,42,1 [?] 1263,3' should be read as: log tan 44°50' = 9.9974734; 1263.3 is the tabular difference per 30''; '29 · 42,1' gives the correction 1221; the result is 9.9975955.
'T/7' is almost certainly T/T0 (or T/𝔗), a ratio of horizontal intensities, not division by 7.
'A-P-p 0953' marks the label A-P-p next to the result ...0953 of the log sum.
'Massenpunkten'/'Massenpunkte' in the prose is most likely 'Flächenstück(e)'; the sentence reads 'Wir denken uns [die Fläche] durch allmähliche Erweiterung von einem Punkte aus erzeugt ...'.
'[-Ostwalt-]' is a struck word, probably 'Offenbar'; 'Eine Fläche' is struck before 'Wenn eine Fläche T'.
In the lemma the first system should read 'durch n1 Querschnitte q1 in ein System T1 von m1 einfach zusammenhängenden Flächenstücken' (subscript 1 on q, not 'T_1 ... q').
The header probably concerns electricity ('... als negative Elektricität'); 'Doppelbrechung' is uncertain.
